notes.text:
Using earlier own n1, there is a complete prescribed NONSKELETAL equation sector on the unchanged analytic carrier. For every c>0 let g=sigma(0), R=exp(-c), and x_c the joint bidisc Gauss point |z_i-1|<=R. For every prescribed 0<=m<=1, mu_(m,c)=(2-m)delta_g+m delta_xc has an actual normalized bounded original-C solution q_(m,c), an actual decreasing G presentation and uniqueness modulo constants among ALL actual G solutions. It attains the FULL dual, with E=-1/3-c m^(3/2)/3 and D=1/6+2c m^(3/2)/3. For m>0 the input is nonskeletal. This solves a narrower equation sector, not unchanged P16.7 or the whole-mass2Dirac.

Construction and genuine gluing. Put xi_i=r_i-floor(r_i) and q0=sum xi_i(1-xi_i)/2-1/4. Positive periodic convolution of its convex quadratic-plus-potential gives actual positive smooth generators and q0 in C. In the injective chart U={|r_i|<1/4}, rho+q0=f1+f2-1/4, fi=log Ai-(1/2)log|zi|, Ai=max(1,|zi|)=max(1,|zi-1|). Write wi=zi-1 and Lc=log max(R,|w1|,|w2|,|w1w2|), vc=Lc-log(A1A2). Extend vc by zero outside U and put qc=q0+vc. If either |wi|>=1, the maximum is AiAj, so vc=0. If both |wi|<1, Ai=1 and vc=log max(R,|w1|,|w2|) in[-c,0]. If either |zi|!=1, ultrametricity gives |wi|>=1. Therefore the correction vanishes whenever tau!=0, and identically on the ORDINARY collar 1/8<max|ri|<1/4. This supplies actual gluing, not just agreement at finite Shilov vertices. Deck units2,3 cause no descent issue because wi are used only on this injective chart and the correction is zero on the collar.

The local potential is rho+qc=Lc-(1/2)log|z1z2|-1/4. The positive constant R keeps Lc continuous. Near a polynomial zero its slot is strictly below R and is omitted; the remaining unit-logarithmic slots have smooth convex-max approximations converging locally uniformly. The other logarithms are actual smooth DD-null unit terms. Hence qc belongs to the ENTIRE original continuous class by minimal-sheaf closure and collar gluing. One has vc(g)=0, vc(xc)=-c, -c<=vc<=0.

Exact products on the ACTUAL analytic space. MA(q0)=2delta_g: DD fi is the integration current of the fixed coordinate Gauss fibre by CLD18.6.2,d1; its self-square is zero, and the product of the two fibres gives delta_g of degree1. The factor2 comes from the two mixed terms. Outside the intersection of the integer coordinate hyperplanes the local baseline is affine or has only one coordinate curvature, so there is no other top mass.

On U, MA(qc)=(DD Lc)^2. At a zero wi, discard its two slots locally and use the one-coordinate dimension rule. Otherwise set bi=log|wi|. The maximum max(-c,b1,b2,b1+b2) has at most two active slots except at(-c,-c) and(0,0): triples involving the constant, product and one single coordinate are dominated by the other single coordinate. With at most two active slots it is locally one unit logarithm plus a one-variable maximum, whose square vanishes by positive smooth approximation. At(-c,-c) the product slot is strictly smaller; apply the exact d2 fibre formula to log max(R,|w1|,|w2|). The coordinate translation is an isomorphism, so its fibre is the singleton xc with coefficient1. At(0,0) the constant is strictly smaller; subtract log|w1w2| to leave log max(1,|w1|^-1,|w2|^-1). The inverse-coordinate isomorphism has singleton unit Gauss fibre g, also coefficient1. Translation by1 preserves the unit bidisc Gauss norm. These same fibre statements exclude every non-Gauss point with the corresponding radii. Outside U the potential is unchanged and has zero baseline top mass. Thus MA(qc)=delta_g+delta_xc globally, on every continuous analytic test, with raw mass2; this is not an unspecified partial mass insertion.

For the mixed product, restrict to the fixed fibre z1=eta1 over H(eta1). The coefficient z1-1 has norm1 at every point, so Lc there is log max(1,|w2|)=log max(1,|z2|). The smooth harmonic correction is unchanged. Fixed-current restriction and the d1 fibre formula on this curve give DD f1 wedge theta_qc=delta_g. Reversing coordinates gives another delta_g; outside U the mixed product equals the zero baseline top measure. Consequently B(q0,qc)=2delta_g. All maps and fibres are on ordinary boundaryless separated equidimensional charts, with degree1; no varying Gauss section or extra extension multiplicity enters.

Put lambda=sqrt(m) and q_(m,c)=(1-lambda)q0+lambda qc. This is an actual convex combination in C. Multilinearity gives MA(q_(m,c))=(1-lambda)^2(2delta_g)+2lambda(1-lambda)(2delta_g)+lambda^2(delta_g+delta_xc)=(2-m)delta_g+m delta_xc, exactly the prescribed input. Its supremum is0 because the correction is nonpositive and zero at a baseline maximum; its range is in[-1/4-c sqrt(m),0]. The sequence q_(m,c)+2^-n decreases continuously to it and has finite lower energy.

The baseline reference/mixed/top moments are-1/6,-1/3,-1/2. Indeed a one-coordinate term has mean int0^1[xi(1-xi)/2-1/8]=-1/24; the reference is2 times torus Lebesgue, the mixed is the sum of two coordinate-circle Lebesgue measures, and the top is2delta_g. Thus E(q0)=-1/3. Actual first variation along q0+lambda vc is int vc MA(q0+lambda vc)=-c lambda^2. Integration yields E=-1/3-c lambda^3/3. Its prescribed-measure moment is-1/2-c lambda^3. Tangent concavity on the ENTIRE C proves full attainment and the stated D, including finiteness of the eligible input. At c=1/8,m=1 this gives the explicit nonskeletal equation MA(q)=delta_g+delta_x, E=-3/8,D=1/4.

Generated uniqueness retains actual representation as an antecedent. For cn decreasing continuously to v with bounded lower energy, compact strict domination between two presentations and E(a+epsilon)=E(a)+2epsilon give canonical limiting energy; apply this to finite convex combinations, then finite unisolvent cubic interpolation gives canonical coefficient limits. For fixed bounded w, Pn(t)=E((1-t)cn+tw), An(t)=E(tcn) give int w MA(cn)=Pn'(0)+An'(1). Dense tests/common positive mass give the canonical weak MA(v)=lambda and finite d=lim int cn MA(cn). Passing bounded tangent inequalities gives D(lambda)<=e-d; monotone convergence in the full dual inequality makes v integrable. The ordered cocycle gives 0<=int(cn-cl)MA(cl)<=3(Ecn-Ecl), l>=n. Pass l then n to infinity to get d=int v lambda and equality D(lambda)=e-int v lambda. The normalized presentation an=cn-sup cn maximizes this dual. Its suprema decrease to finite sup v by nested compact superlevel sets and Ecn<=2sup cn. If lambda=MA(q_(m,c)), midpoint and n1 full-point moduli force v-s=q_(m,c) at all full points. They are dense. USC of the already decreasing v-s rules out values below continuous q. Finite affinoid Shilov bounds, followed by shrinking neighborhoods, rule out values above q. Thus v=q+constant at EVERY point of X.

For any normalized NONORDERED maximizing net for this target, coercivity bounds its tail energies and midpoint gives I(ai,q)<=4epsilon_i. The moduli identify its finite full-point tuple with q, its genuine weak MA limit with the target, and its energy with E(q). Finite Shilov maximum bounds and continuity of q identify its canonical ordinary upper relaxation with this already constructed actual original-C representative. Every fast sequence has J=K=0 and the Borel limit equals q at the two full target atoms. Positivity is not assigned to its raw Borel limsup at remaining points. This is a complete nonordered representation result for this sector only.

There is also an exact obstruction to stretching this segment. For lambda>1 choose a in K with0<|a|<R and restrict to the actual curve w2=a near the unit Gauss point of w1. There A2=1 and Lc=log|w1|. Up to actual smooth harmonic terms, the local potential of q0+lambda vc is (1-lambda)log max(1,|w1|)+lambda log|w1|. Its DD is(1-lambda)delta_eta1, a negative curve atom. Pullback of a member of the entire minimal continuous class has positive DD, so this extended weight is not in C. The formal square would need lambda=sqrt2 to reach2delta_xc; this route fails. Using earlier own n1 and n2, domination by a fixed actual bounded MA measure eliminates the prescribed-measure integral defect, WITHOUT asserting analytic recognition. Let mu be ANY positive raw-mass2 Radon measure with mu<=A MA(w), w in original C bounded and A finite. Equal masses give A>=1. Write Bw=D(MA(w))=E(w)-int w MA(w), finite by bounded tangent concavity. Then D(mu)<=A(1+Bw)+(3/2)A^2 Bw<infinity, so these arbitrary-support inputs are eligible for the ORIGINAL FULL dual.

Proof of the bound. Normalize a by sup0 and put C=-E(a), A0=int(-a)theta^2<=1, q0=Q_theta(a), q1=Q_theta_a(a). Cubic differentiation gives C=A0+2q0/3+q1/3 and -E(ta)=tA0+t^2(1-t/3)q0+t^3 q1/3<=t+(3/2)t^2 C. Apply the full dual Bw to ta and divide by t. Optimizing t=min(1,sqrt(2Bw/(3C))), with the zero cases treated by limits, gives int(-a)MA(w)<=1+Bw+sqrt(6Bw C). Domination yields Fmu(a)<=-C+A(1+Bw)+A sqrt(6Bw C). Maximizing the scalar quadratic in sqrt C proves the claimed bound. This proof does not need skeletal support, absolute continuity of mu against a geometric volume form or a smooth positivity margin.

Every normalized full-dual maximizing family is Cauchy in L1(mu), with a family-independent limit. Coercivity puts late terms in a common C-energy sublevel. Midpoint gives I(ai,aj)<=4(epsilon_i+epsilon_j), and the fixed-w absolute modulus in n1, multiplied by A, tends to0. Completeness of L1(mu) supplies a limit; comparison of two families on their product indices proves independence, without assuming countable cofinality of nets. In particular every maximizing sequence has uniform integrability of its negative functions, after handling its finitely many initial terms.

More precisely, for EVERY fast sequence with the n1 diagonal estimates, select k so normalized w lies in C_(C+k). For j>=k, int h_j MA(w)<=sum_(n>=j)2^-4n, h_j=sum_(n>=j)|a_(n+1)-an|, by countable Tonelli. Its exceptional set N is MA(w)-null and therefore mu-null. Outside N the actual pointwise limit u satisfies |aj-u|<=h_j. Consequently, for every sufficiently late j,
int|aj-u|mu <= A sum_(n>=j)2^-4n = (16A/15)2^-4j.
This proves actual mu-integrability and L1 convergence to the actual Borel u, not just signed integral convergence. Its integral is e-D(mu), so J=int u mu-(e-Dmu)=0. The bounded truncations converge in L1 and the negative functions are uniformly integrable: for vn=-an,v=-u, (vn-T)+ <=|vn-v|+(v-T)+; first control a late tail, then finitely many initial integrable functions. Thus both requirements in the earlier exact loss split are supplied. No positivity/energy/MA is assigned to u, no statement u in C/G is inferred, and K or nu=mu need not follow from this argument.

For the specified x=x_(1/8), n2 gives an EXPLICIT actual bounded q with MA(q)=delta_g+delta_x and full dual1/4. Hence2delta_x<=2MA(q), taking A=2. The ORIGINAL whole-mass nonskeletal Dirac now satisfies J=0 for every fast family, int|aj-u|2delta_x <=(32/15)2^-4j eventually, and all normalized maximizing families have the same L1(2delta_x) limit. Evaluating q at the target, E(q)=-3/8 and q(x)=-3/8, gives D(2delta_x)>=3/8. The domination bound gives D(2delta_x)<=2(1+1/4)+(3/2)*4*(1/4)=4. These are rigorous bounds, not an exact dual computation. The old tiny projection-gap bound is strengthened substantially.
